activity_context.topic_title: The Sum of a Finite Geometric Series

feedback.problem:
The first term of a geometric series is $10$, the last term is $\frac{10}{81}$, and the common ratio is $\frac{1}{3}.$ What is the sum of this series?

Express your answer as a fraction (do not round your answer).

The sum of this series is
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a geometric series, the sum of the first $N$ terms is given by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r},
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term of the series and $r$ is the common ratio. In our case, we have ${a}_{1}=10$ and $r=\frac{1}{3}.$

We must determine $N$ (the index of the last term). To do this, we use the fact that

$$
{a}_{N}={a}_{1}\cdot {r}^{N-1}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{10}{81} & =10\cdot {(\frac{1}{3})}^{N-1} \\ \frac{1}{81} & ={(\frac{1}{3})}^{N-1} \\ \frac{1}{{3}^{4}} & ={(\frac{1}{3})}^{N-1} \\ {(\frac{1}{3})}^{4} & ={(\frac{1}{3})}^{N-1} \\ 4 & =N-1 \\ N & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, if we substitute ${a}_{1}=10,$ $r=\frac{1}{3},$ and $N=5$ into the formula for ${S}_{N},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{5} & =10\cdot \frac{(1-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{5})}{(1-\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =\frac{10}{(\frac{2}{3})}\cdot \frac{{3}^{5}-1}{{3}^{5}} \\  & =15\cdot \frac{242}{243} \\  & =\frac{1\,210}{81}.\end{aligned}
$$
